choices: a feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment
a change made by choosing a pet
s6.evolution.adaptation.answer: a feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment
s6.evolution.adaptation.hint: It helps an organism fit its surroundings.
s6.evolution.adaptation.explain: An adaptation is a feature that gives a living thing an advantage in its environment.

choices: how living things have changed over time
what the weather will be tomorrow
the exact colour of every extinct animal
how to grow a plant instantly
s6.evolution.adaptation.answer: how living things have changed over time
s6.evolution.adaptation.hint: Fossils provide evidence from the past.
s6.evolution.adaptation.explain: Fossils provide evidence about organisms that lived long ago and how life has changed.

s6.evolution.adaptation.prompt: Why might a polar bear's thick fur be useful?
choices: it helps keep the bear warm in a cold environment
it makes the bear invisible everywhere
it lets the bear breathe underwater
s6.evolution.adaptation.answer: it helps keep the bear warm in a cold environment
s6.evolution.adaptation.explain: Thick fur is an adaptation that reduces heat loss in cold places.

s6.evolution.adaptation.prompt: What do offspring inherit from their parents?
s6.evolution.adaptation.hint: Think about features passed through genes.
s6.evolution.adaptation.explain: Offspring inherit characteristics from their parents, although they are not identical copies.

s6.electricity.voltage.prompt: What usually happens when more cells are added to a series circuit?
s6.electricity.voltage.hint: Cells provide the push for current.
s6.electricity.voltage.explain: Adding cells in series increases the total voltage.

s6.electricity.voltage.prompt: What may happen to a lamp when the voltage increases?
s6.electricity.voltage.hint: More voltage can provide more energy to the lamp.
s6.electricity.voltage.explain: A higher voltage can make a lamp brighter, within its safe limits.

s6.electricity.voltage.prompt: Which component can make a sound in a circuit?
s6.electricity.voltage.hint: Its name tells you what it does.
s6.electricity.voltage.explain: A buzzer changes electrical energy into sound.

s6.electricity.voltage.prompt: What should be kept the same in a fair test of bulb brightness?
choices: the bulb and circuit arrangement except for the number of cells
everything including the number of cells
s6.electricity.voltage.answer: the bulb and circuit arrangement except for the number of cells
s6.electricity.voltage.hint: Change one variable at a time.
s6.electricity.voltage.explain: A fair test changes only the number of cells and keeps other variables controlled.

counting every animal in a habitat
s6.living.classification.answer: putting living things into groups using shared features
s6.living.classification.hint: Scientists organise organisms by similarities and differences.
s6.living.classification.explain: Classification groups living things according to common characteristics.

s6.living.classification.prompt: Which group has feathers and lays eggs?
s6.living.classification.hint: Think of a robin or an owl.
s6.living.classification.explain: Birds have feathers and reproduce by laying eggs.

s6.living.classification.prompt: Which feature is common to mammals?
choices: they feed their young with milk
s6.living.classification.answer: they feed their young with milk
s6.living.classification.hint: It is a defining mammal characteristic.
s6.living.classification.explain: Female mammals produce milk to feed their young.

s6.living.classification.prompt: Why might scientists use a classification key?
choices: to identify an organism from its observable features
s6.living.classification.answer: to identify an organism from its observable features
